title: Quantum Entanglement in Variational Quantum Classification for Breast Cancer Diagnosis
authors: Zineb Hazmoun, Zoubida Sakhi, Mohamed Bennai
abstract: This study looks at how the entangling structure of a variational quantum classifier (VQC) relates to its performance in breast cancer diagnosis, using the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (WDBC) dataset. We tested three three-qubit configurations that share the same EfficientSU2 ansatz, COBYLA optimizer, and stratified five-fold cross-validation, but differ in their entangling structure: a single- repetition Ising-type coupling (A), a two-repetition linear Ising-type coupling (B), and a fully connected Heisenberg-type coupling (C). Entanglement was measured with the von Neumann entropy and the Wootters concurrence. From A to C, the mean entropy rose from 0.40 to 0.71, accuracy rose from 92.98% to 93.68%, and F1-score rose from 90.32% to 91.28%. Configuration C was also the most stable across folds. However, the fold-level correlations between entanglement and performance were weak and not significant. Richer topologies also increase circuit expressivity, so the two effects cannot be fully separated. These results show an association, not a proven causal link, between entangling structure and VQC performance.
summary: This paper tests how varying the entanglement structure within a Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) affects its ability to diagnose breast cancer. By comparing three distinct three-qubit circuit topologies, the authors found that richer entanglement structures correlate with better classification metrics. However, they caution that this correlation is not statistically significant, suggesting that circuit expressivity is a complex factor beyond just entanglement.
main_problem: The study investigates the relationship between the specific entangling structure of a Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) and its diagnostic performance when applied to breast cancer data.
main_result: While increasing the entangling structure (from Ising to Heisenberg type) correlated with higher entanglement and better performance metrics, the statistical correlation between entanglement and performance was found to be weak and not significant.
method: The authors compared three three-qubit VQC configurations (A, B, C) using the EfficientSU2 ansatz and evaluated performance via five-fold cross-validation.
model_or_system: The model is a Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) applied to the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (WDBC) dataset. The configurations differ in their entangling structure: single-repetition Ising, two-repetition linear Ising, and fully connected Heisenberg-type coupling.
key_observables: Von Neumann entropy, Wootters concurrence, Accuracy, and F1-score.
important_parameters: Three-qubit system, COBYLA optimizer, stratified five-fold cross-validation.
main_assumptions: The observed correlation is an association, not a proven causal link, because changing the structure simultaneously alters expressivity, connectivity, and depth.
figures_summary: Figures conceptually link QML for healthcare to circuit structure and entanglement; one figure shows the increasing trend of entanglement measures (EE, Conc) and performance metrics (Accuracy, F1-score) from A to C.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem (QML for diagnosis), details the methodology (VQC setup, three configurations A, B, C, and entanglement/performance measurements), presents results showing increasing trends, and concludes with a cautious interpretation regarding causality.
why_interesting: It applies quantum circuit analysis (entanglement measures) to a practical machine learning task, providing insights into how hardware connectivity constraints (Hamiltonian structure) impact quantum algorithm performance.
